summary:
Hitting and bullpen_fatigue remain the categories to lean on across the board — every rating from R1 to R4 is riding a 4-game winning streak on hitting (R4 hottest at 81%, +28.3pts over baseline) and bullpen_fatigue is cooking even harder on R4 (+19.7pts) and R1/R2/R3 alike (+18.7pts, 65% at n=26). SP is the one category to fade everywhere — a 5-game losing streak across all four ratings, with R4's SP specifically flagged COLD at -5.2pts. Bullpen sits HOT across the slate too (62% at n=26, +9.4pts for R1-R3, +6.8pts for R4), so when bullpen and hitting line up on the same side, that's as strong a signal as this model offers right now.

Today's two-game card is about as clean as it gets: both games show full consensus across all four ratings. CLE @ TBR is the stronger side by average delta — TBR graded +1.66 to +2.02 across every rating, with R2 showing the biggest edge at +2.02. That lines up perfectly with team trends: TBR is 70% (42-18, n=60) when the model likes them, and 72% in strong-play spots for +22.0u on the season — one of the best team-when-liked profiles on the board. Rasmussen over Griffin only reinforces the lean. LAD @ MIL is consensus too, but the deltas are thin (-0.27 to -0.37 across ratings), signaling a much softer edge toward LAD — worth monitoring but not pounding. LAD's season team-when-liked number is strong (71%, 80% in strong plays for +27.0u), but with deltas this small and MIL itself a 67% team-when-liked play (26-12 strong, +17.0u), this one reads more coinflip than conviction. Prioritize TBR as the unit play of the day, and treat MIL-LAD as a smaller-stake lean until the gap widens.
